reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not directly address the key premises. E1 discusses general HEA compositions and properties but does not confirm a single-phase BCC structure, lattice distortions, or dislocation mechanisms for WTaTiVZr. E2 reports creep behavior of TaTiVWZr and HfTaTiVZr at much lower temperatures (298–573 K) and does not provide evidence for the proposed high-temperature dislocation-mediated toughening mechanism in WTaTiVZr.
premises: Equimolar WTaTiVZr forms a single-phase BCC structure with homogeneous elemental distribution.
Uniform refractory elements in WTaTiVZr introduce significant lattice distortions.
Lattice distortions modify dislocation core structures and lower barriers for dislocation motion.
Enhanced dislocation mobility mitigates brittleness, improving plastic strain and toughness over pure W.
The mechanism operates at high temperatures (>1000°C) where thermally activated dislocation processes dominate.
